sentences.text:
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
The essential grievance of the Petitioners is as to non-disbursal of compensation amount for the acquired land and also against disbursal of a part of compensation in favour of one of their brothers.

Learned counsel for the Petitioners vehemently argues that his clients happen to be the owners of the subject property which has now been acquired and therefore, their claim for payment of compensation has to be adjudged by the answering Respondent - KIADB in accordance with law before the compensation is disbursed to the persons who have been wrongly shown to be owners of the subject land in terms of the award in question there being no such consideration of their Representation, the Petitioners are knocking at the doors of Writ Court, argues their counsel.

2. After service, the 1st Respondent is represented by learned AGA; 2nd & 3rd Respondents are represented by their respective Panel Counsel; now impleaded 4th Respondent is represented by Mr. Nitin Prasad, a private counsel.
All they oppose the Petition contending that ordinarily in disbursing the compensation what the acquiring body is to see is only the contents of the award and names figuring therein.

If others are aggrieved by the award because of non-inclusion of their names therein, ordinarily the right remedy is to approach the civil Court seeking adjudication of complex issues, which cannot be adjudged by the Writ Court in its limited supervisory jurisdiction.
This Court broadly agrees with the said submission and therefore, is inclined to relegates the Petitioners to the civil Court.

In view of the above, Writ Petition is disposed off reserving liberty to the Petitioners to approach the jurisdictional civil Court for working out their grievance as has been reflected in their subject Representation.
In that regard, all contentions are kept open.
Since the Petitioners are being relegated to an alternate forum.
Justice of the case warrants that the compensation shall not be disbursed in respect of the subject land for a period of two weeks.
However, the civil Court shall not take note of this reprieve while considering any application for interim relief in the suit in contemplation.
No costs.
